scope: Only review-packets C01-C08 production snapshots/requirements/patches and I01-I04 interviews. Qualitative independent review; no policy ranking.

reviewer.nominal_anonymity: Candidate labels only; no mapping, policy, grades, study results, previous juries or conversation outcomes read. This is an instruction boundary, not OS-enforced confinement.

limitations: Qualitative evidence, not sole-authority correctness or benchmark claim.
No production files changed; no provider workflows, hosted model calls, external services, new benchmark, publication or large test suite.
Packet snapshots omit dependency/test fixtures; visible unittest commands not run because reading outside the packet is disallowed.
All production files parsed as Python; narrow AST-extracted function checks use stdlib-only namespaces and stubs, not integration execution.
Source locations and behavior findings are bounded to packet content. No definite defect found does not certify absence of defects.
Scripted interview ledger is incomplete intent and keyword matching can miss valid phrasing; asked questions, received answers and readiness assessed separately.

observations.observation: Numeric CLI input has a strict positive finite validator; optional runtime budget maps None/off to disabled; new checkpoint serializes disabled as null.

Disabled run_phase builds no deadline, waits with timeout None, and bypasses steering on TimeoutError. Resume uses a distinct off marker for explicit disable and preserves persisted value when override is omitted.

complexity.observation: The strict/optional/default resolvers and resume marker add several small adapters, but the distinctions serve numeric-only CLI validation and omitted-versus-disabled resume behavior. No clearly unnecessary machinery identified.

observations.observation: Driver ownership filter suppresses a child thread terminal and a legacy nonactive terminal before the run loop; active legacy terminal remains accepted. Agent receipt capture also checks turn identity and ownership while progress is still fed.
Final receipt fallback and finally-based driver cleanup remain present.

interpretation_risks.observation: A completion on the coordinator thread with a stale turn ID is still returned and causes the run loop to raise. This preserves the prepatch wrong-turn guard, but the broad phrase only active thread/turn may establish outcome could instead require ignoring stale coordinator turns. Not classified as a confirmed miss without resolving that interpretation.

complexity.observation: One ownership helper reused for terminal and receipt selection; no substantial unrelated complexity.

observations.observation: Both event-loop paths accept only the active turn and reject a conflicting thread identity from params or completed_turn. Legacy active-turn completion is accepted; stale coordinator completion is ignored.
Existing receipt capture remains scoped to exact thread and turn; final receipt fallback and driver cleanup remain intact.

complexity.observation: Single boolean helper; examining both possible thread containers is conservative and inexpensive. No clearly unnecessary expansion identified.

observations.observation: Filters child terminals in both polling paths; accepts active legacy completion with no thread identity; an additional terminal-is-None guard prevents later matching terminals replacing an already selected terminal while waiting for steer acknowledgement.
Scoped receipt capture, final receipt fallback and finally cleanup remain present.

interpretation_risks.observation: Stale coordinator turn IDs raise rather than being ignored. This is the prepatch guard, with the same unresolved broad-requirement interpretation as C02. If params.threadId and completed_turn.threadId conflict, params takes precedence; the packet does not establish that such contradictory events are supported.

complexity.observation: A small helper plus a terminal replacement guard is proportionate; no clearly unnecessary machinery identified.

observations.observation: Uses an identity sentinel for explicit resume disable, converts it to None for checkpoint persistence, and keeps omission separate. Disabled runtime has no deadline and guards steering; CLI numeric off is rejected.
Checkpoint validator permits null; new-question checkpoint passes the optional resolver. CLI mutually exclusive group separates numeric and disable flags.

complexity.observation: Custom sentinel class is more ceremony than a bare object but its repr aids debugging; repeated normalization around resume is local and justified by retaining omitted/disabled distinction. No material unnecessary complexity found.

observations.observation: Disabled runtime waits without deadline/steering. Resume normalizes the sentinel to null but separately records whether an override was supplied, so numeric override and disabled override both persist.
CLI uses manual mutual-exclusion validation and a budget parsing helper; numeric off is rejected, numeric CLI overrides environment off, omission on resume preserves saved choice.

complexity.observation: Custom sentinel and explicit override boolean encode the necessary third state. Manual conflict validation duplicates an argparse capability but is a minor local choice, not material overengineering.

observations.observation: Both event-loop paths filter child thread completion and accept only matching active-turn legacy completion. Existing receipt selection and cleanup are preserved.

interpretation_risks.observation: Stale coordinator turn IDs retain the prepatch RuntimeError behavior. Helper reads thread identity only from params; nested-only threadId attribution is not established by the packet requirements, so this is not counted as a confirmed defect.

complexity.observation: One dict-or-None helper reused across both paths; no clearly unnecessary machinery identified.

confirmed_missed_requirements.requirement: --soft-phase-budget-seconds remains restricted to positive finite numbers; invalid input is rejected before provider invocation.
confirmed_missed_requirements.finding: The general resolver accepts string off as disabled, and parse sends the numeric CLI flag through that resolver. --soft-phase-budget-seconds off scope fixture returns a disabled None budget instead of rejecting invalid numeric input. On resume the same None is interpreted as no override, so it may silently preserve a positive saved budget.
confirmed_missed_requirements.verification: AST-extracted production parse and resolver returned None for --soft-phase-budget-seconds off; no provider/import execution.

observations.observation: Correct disable flag uses a resume marker; runtime None disables deadline/steering and checkpoint validator accepts null. Explicit positive numeric CLI overrides environment off.

interpretation_risks.observation: Omitted resume option still evaluates environment default before discarding it. An invalid environment value therefore prevents resuming even if the saved budget is valid; whether unused environment inputs must be rejected is not explicit enough to count as a second confirmed miss.

complexity.observation: Reusing one permissive resolver for runtime and numeric-only CLI conflates different contracts. Duplicate prevalidation/normalization on resume is minor; the main problem is insufficient separation of input semantics.

readiness.observation: Reports ready=false in every round. Core routing choices are settled; full-scope readiness cannot be decided from these source facts alone. No false ready claim.
